title: Why Morgan Stanley Banker Seeks Female Role Models - Nina Godiwalla
description: In Chapter 14 of 14, ex-Morgan Stanley investment banker and "Suits: A Woman on Wall Street" author Nina Godiwalla shares why female role models are so critical in building a corporate finance career. Godiwalla faces challenges and seeks counsel in mid-to-senior level female bankers who make themselves available to support more junior peers. Godiwalla goes on to found a Morgan Stanley Women's Committee to help those needing guidance and support.  View more at http://www.captureyourflag.com

asr.full_text: How have female role models and mentors given you strength and support on your journey today? I've lived in different cities, I've been in different countries. There are moments in my life where I'm very very aware I'm a woman. And one of the most striking examples is when I was in investment banking and I didn't have this awareness of being, usually it's like there's different things that stand out, depending on what environment you're in. And for me, I was in a group – I was the only woman in my group for a while when I was in investment banking, and it´s a completely different culture that I wasn't very familiar with. That was one of the times in life I realized, I really need – I need somebody that's done this. I need a woman around me to help me kind of navigate the system." And I would say before that in life, I had it necessarily – I was not seeking out women mentors. And when I was at college getting a finance degree at UT, there wasn't an attitude of here, let me find other women. But being thrown into that environment that was so different, suddenly I really desperately – quite desperately – really sought other women. And what was interesting to me about the investment banking world is that there were definitely the women that had been there. There were so few that had been there for a very long time. But I found there was very different perspectives of women. Some people were, yes, let me help you, let me help you, how can we do this, what is that, how can we work, how can I be your mentor, and then there were other people you've got to rough it out, were, yes, let me help you. Let me help you. How can we do this? How can we work? How can I be your mentor? There were other people that said, you've got to rough it out. This is what it is. We don't need to talk about the things that are happening. If this isn't working for you, just keep pushing through. Put your head down and keep pushing through. And I gravitated towards people that that is actually something I wanted to discuss and talk about different things. And I couldn't have made it through in a lot of ways without those mentors. The experience I had was in corporate finance, which was a kind of experience where it's a little notorious for keeping you working all the time. And you don't really necessarily have that time to reflect and think about things. I started Morgan Stanley Women's Committee because I found people were looking for some guidance and they just had no idea where to go because they would look to the people right about a year ahead of them and those people were there was an analyst program and those people were so busy and then the senior women were just they were so senior that and there were so few of them that you just wouldn't go call one of them up and say hey I had a bad day today can I talk to you so it was really kind of bringing a group of women together is what I started because I found that was the way people were were going to help get through. Because a lot of women would start coming to me with their issues, and this was happening and this was kind of stuff was happening, and so I thought why don't we bring this group together.
